As of 140 PM Sunday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... Overall light rain lifting north across central NC 
will continue to linger much of the day before exiting this evening. 

An area of overall light rain is currently shifting to the north 
through central NC. MRMS is suggesting that there has been decent 
area of over 0.25 inches so far today, located over the eastern 
Piedmont, the Sandhills, and the southern Coastal Plain. While much 
of this area is also estimated at being over 0.5 inch, there was 
also an area with more moderate rainfall this morning which led to a 
swath of higher rainfall totals from northern Hoke county north into 
Lee county. The highest totals in this area are being estimated in 
excess of 2.5 inches. Additionally, as of 1:30 PM, RDU has measured 
0.71 inches of rain today. 

This area is associated with a pair of low pressure systems which 
are currently being shifted north along the southeast and mid-
Atlantic coast. As the shortwave continues to move though, the area 
of rain should be shifted eastward out of the region. It appears the 
rain should exit our Coastal Plain counties around midnight tonight. 
Many models are suggesting that there could be an additional 0.5 to 
1.5 inches of rain between 1PM to 1AM in the eastern Piedmont, 
Sandhills, and Coastal Plain, with some suggestion of a few higher 
pockets as well. Due to the overall light stratiform nature of the 
rain, flooding should not be a large threat, however cannot rule out 
some nuisance flooding if a pocket of more moderate rain moves over 
a poor drainage area. 



KEY MESSAGE 2... Below-normal temperatures through mid-week, 
followed by another low pressure system developing off the Southeast 
US coast and lifting northward across the region.

In the wake of the coastal low this weekend, a cold front is 
forecast to move across the area Mon night. A Canadian high will 
strengthen as it migrates ewd across the upr MS Valley, Great Lakes, 
and Northeast US, ridging swd across central NC through mid-week. As 
the high moves across the Northeast US and Canadian Maritimes on Wed 
and Thu, an area of low pressure will develop along/off the 
Southeast US coast. There are still timing and track differences 
amongst the available guidance, but the low should deepen as it 
lifts nwd, either along the Carolina and Mid-Atlantic coasts (EC) or 
across the Carolinas and Mid-Atlantic (GFS), Wed night and Thu. The 
low should lift away from the area Thu night/Fri, with high pressure 
again building into the region in its wake. 

Aloft, a leading s/w, which is expected to come onshore along the 
Pacific Coast this evening, will swing across the srn Plains and lwr 
MS Valley Tue/Tue night as a nrn stream s/w drops ssewd across the 
Plains. The pair of lows will likely interact with one another, the 
latter eventually picking up the former as they progress ewd through 
the end of the week. The leading, more progressive s/w may briefly 
close off as it swings ewd across the Deep South then lifts newd 
across the Southeast US and Mid-Atlantic Wed and Thu, consequently 
slowing the ewd progression of the trailing s/w, which should deepen 
and drift ewd across the Midwest. The leading s/w should lift away 
from the area Thu night/Fri, while the trailing s/w progresses ewd 
across the OH Valley. Model solutions still vary wrt the track and 
timing of each s/w, as well as how exactly they will interact with 
one another.

Temperatures: With the strengthening Canadian high ridging into the 
area Mon night-Wed, expect strong CAA from the NE and crashing low-
level thicknesses, with a CAD airmass in place Tue night/Wed. With 
rain overspreading the area on Wed and falling into that airmass 
(should it not have time to erode), highs could be lower than 
currently forecast. For now, expect below normal highs on Tue, mid 
to upr 50s. There will likely be a larger range and stronger 
gradient in highs, ranging from around 50 degrees NW to low 60s SE 
on Wed, though as noted above that is subject to change. 
Additionally, expect winds/gust to increase Tue and moreso Wed as 
the low approaches, making it feel much colder. Gusts of 25-35 mph 
are expected across much of the area Wed aft through Thu.

Precipitation: The cold front passage Mon night may be largely dry, 
however a few showers/sprinkles are possible. The higher chance for 
rain will be with the coastal low Wed and Thu, as models continue to 
be in good agreement wrt rain chances as the system approaches and 
moves across the area. It still appears earliest onset should be on 
Wed across the south, spreading northward through the day, possibly 
holding off until Wed eve along the VA border. Highest chances area-
wide are Wed eve through Thu morn. Amounts generally ranging from 
three quarters of an inch to an inch and a half or more from west to 
east across the area, though uncertainty in amounts remains.

Mainly dry and calm weather is expected Saturday.
